versions.short: The bill would allow landlords, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and utility and phone companies to report to credit bureaus how consumers pay their rent, utilities, and phone bills, but only the payment and billing terms rather than details of how much energy or service someone uses. It would also stop energy utilities from reporting a balance as late when the customer is current on an agreed payment plan, such as a deferred payment or debt forgiveness program. The bill would protect those furnishers from liability under the Fair Credit Reporting Act when they follow these rules. Finally, it would require the Government Accountability Office to report to Congress within two years on how this reporting affects consumers and how reporting cash flow data would affect credit scores.
